html:
The map's label (spelled "fichers" there) for the peoples of the Columbia Plateau, the dry interior between the Cascade Mountains and the Rockies, in what is now Washington, Oregon, Idaho and British Columbia. The map shows them from 1500 BCE to 1530.

Life followed the seasons:

  • salmon running up the Columbia River and its branches, caught with spears and dip nets from wooden platforms;
  • roots such as camas bulbs and bitterroot, dug in spring and baked in earth ovens;
  • deer, elk and mountain sheep hunted in the hills;
  • winter villages of pit houses dug partly into the ground.

Celilo Falls on the Columbia was one of the great fishing places of North America for thousands of years, and also a trade fair where coast and interior peoples met.

Salishan peoples lived in the north, such as the Okanagan and the Salish and Kootenai. Sahaptin peoples lived in the south, such as the Nez Perce, Yakama and Umatilla.

Horses reached the Plateau in the early 1700s, and the Nez Perce became famous horse breeders. Lewis and Clark passed through in 1805. Celilo Falls was drowned by a dam in 1957.
